Sam (Product): Quick heads-up: we need a compact list of launch gate checkpoints tied to customer promises. Thinking: SLA language, pricing commitment, support response SLAs, and docs/videos. Keep it short so sales can hand to pilot customers.
June (Eng): For SLAs we should be explicit about measurement windows. Propose: availability measured monthly, p99 latency measured over rolling 30d, but customer-facing guarantees are on a 7d rolling window for early pilots.
Ravi (SRE): agree on measurement windows. Also important: define allowed maintenance windows (e.g., weekly 2-hour window UTC-04:00). If we have emergency maintenance we'll notify 1 hour ahead and provide a status blurb.
Lena (Finance): For pilot customers we usually do a billing holdback: invoice at 50% of expected consumption for first 30 days, then true-up. Want that in the customer commitment doc.
Maya (Docs): I'll draft a one-pager customer promise template: bullets for SLA, support tiers, billing terms, and an FAQ about fallbacks. Need exact wording for SLA numbers.
Sam (Product): Proposed public-facing commitment (short): "99.9% monthly availability; p95 latency under 150ms for low-latency tier; priority support response < 4h business hours." Thoughts?
June (Eng): 99.9% monthly availability is reasonable for GA if we scope out cross-region fallbacks. For low-latency tier p95 < 150ms is tight — depends on model & region. We should qualify by model family and region in the doc.
Ravi (SRE): Also include the operational safety-net: automatic fallback to compatible model variant when latency or errors spike, documented rollback steps, and a canary slice (10%) for any rollout for 24h before global change.
Owen (Support): Support commitments: First-response (ack) target: Priority=1: 1h, Priority=2: 4h, Priority=3: 1 business day. Escalation: if unresolved > 6h for P1 escalate to SRE oncall. I'll put these in the support playbook.
Sam (Product): Good. Also add a small customer-facing incident blurb example: "We detected increased latency and routed traffic to a compatible model variant to preserve availability; working on root cause." Maya can you add that to the FAQ.
Maya (Docs): Yup. Also will add a short how-to for customers to opt into burst pricing vs reserved capacity, and the visible dashboard indicators for their current routing tier.
June (Eng): We need a concise set of alert rules for the SLOs so Ops knows when to page vs when to notify only. Example rule I suggest adding to runbook:
```yaml
- name: P99 high latency
  expr: api_request_latency_seconds{job="inference",model_family="lowlatency"} > 0.35
  for: 5m
  severity: page
- name: Error rate spike
  expr: rate(api_request_errors_total[3m]) > 0.05
  for: 3m
  severity: page
- name: Availability degradation (notice)
  expr: sum(rate(api_request_success_total[1h])) / sum(rate(api_request_total[1h])) < 0.995
  for: 60m
  severity: notify
```
Ravi (SRE): We'll wire those into PagerDuty with playbook links. For canary failures we will auto-abort rollouts at 10% failure delta and create a P1 if rollback doesn't restore baseline within 15m.
Lena (Finance): For pricing promises: any "no-surprise" pricing commitments must include a delta clause: we reserve the right to adjust rates for quantization/accelerator pass-throughs with 30d notice. For pilots we'll add explicit exceptions.
Sam (Product): Action list: Maya -> publish customer-promise draft + FAQ, June -> add gating qualifiers for each model-family, Ravi -> finalize alert rules + PD mappings, Owen -> support playbook + incident blurb, Lena -> formalize pilot billing holdback language. Please ack here when done.
